reports.title: Astra: strong mockups and working user flows
reports.configuration: GPT-6 Astra at medium thinking effort
reports.summary: Astra placed second overall and led mockups. Reviewers found complete shopping interactions, but flagged small text and unintended changes during refinement.
reports.limitation: A staged landing-page study; visual preference and functional completeness are separate outcomes.

reports.title: Different models led different design stages
reports.summary: Sol led ideation, Opus mockups, and Fable refinement. Six designers assessed three product briefs through three stages.
reports.limitation: Only nine prompts; stage-specific preferences should not become a universal model ranking. Sol used Codex CLI.

reports.title: Opus 5: layout and readability needed rework
reports.summary: Nine designers reviewed 20 landing pages. Opus drew substantial layout and readability criticism, while brand fit and originality attracted fewer flags.
reports.limitation: Five briefs, older model versions; annotation counts are not independent failure rates.

reports.title: Prompt and workflow changes reversed design rankings
reports.summary: Sol led three brief-based evaluations; Claude models moved ahead when work became staged visual design. This supports comparing whole workflows, including prompts and harnesses.
reports.limitation: Model lineup, evaluators, assets and harness changed between evaluations; this does not isolate a causal prompt effect.

reports.title: Ad-image strengths differed by production stage
reports.summary: Muse Image led overall, while ChatGPT Images 2.0 led ideation. Designers compared nine prompts across three ad campaigns and three production stages.
reports.limitation: Professional creative preference on a small campaign set; these are image models, not chat-model scores.

reports.title: Image preference did not guarantee client readiness
reports.summary: GenPeach won 71% of blind votes against eight rivals, but just 49% of its images were rated client-ready.
reports.limitation: Commissioned by GenPeach; anchor-only matchups, 100 photography briefs, no retries. Refusals were excluded rather than counted as losses.

reports.title: Sol and Astra: published web-app cloning costs
reports.summary: Sol scored 12.6% at $25.35/run; Astra scored 17.5% at $207.27/run.
reports.limitation: Nine apps; partial replication, unequal spend.

reports.title: Higher effort sharply increased small-game cost
reports.configuration: Claude Code 2.1.295; three runs per effort setting
reports.summary: Opus averaged $0.26 at medium versus $5.33 at max for the same brick-breaker brief. Every tested Opus and Sonnet game passed the stated play checks.
reports.limitation: One task, three repeats per setting. API-equivalent costs on a subscription, not incremental cash charges.
reports.costContext: Opus medium; average list-price usage estimate reported by Claude Code.

reports.title: Three small games passed on all three Claude models
reports.configuration: Claude Code; three games × three models × five runs
reports.summary: All 45 games passed automated play tests. Median API-equivalent cost was $0.015 for Haiku, $0.13 for Sonnet and $0.28 for Opus; Sonnet was fastest.
reports.limitation: Small single-file games. Correctness checks do not establish visual quality or larger-project reliability.
reports.costContext: Haiku median/game; subscription-run usage valued at API list prices.

reports.title: Cheaper models were competitive on bounded bug fixes
reports.configuration: Claude Code 2.1.295; medium effort; 25 bugs, three runs/model/bug
reports.summary: Clean fixes were 52/75 for Haiku, 49/75 for Sonnet and 54/75 for Opus. Haiku's average usage estimate was $0.019 versus Opus's $0.38.
reports.limitation: Haiku–Opus differences were not statistically significant. Public parser/data-library bugs; results exclude many larger-system failure modes.
reports.costContext: Haiku mean/run; subscription usage at API list prices.

reports.title: Fable 5.2 and Opus 5.5 tied on clean fixes
reports.configuration: Claude Code 2.1.322; medium effort; 125 planned runs
reports.summary: Fable 5.2 and Opus each made 37 clean fixes in 50 attempts. Average API-equivalent cost was $0.73 for Fable 5.2 and $0.40 for Opus.
reports.limitation: Twenty-five bounded bugs; one or two repeats per model. Interrupted attempts were rerun; larger tasks may differ.
reports.costContext: Fable 5.2 mean/run; subscription usage at API list prices.

reports.title: Worker model choice changed delegated-search cost
reports.configuration: Claude Code 2.1.318; 12 code-search questions × three runs/setting
reports.summary: Using Haiku for Explore workers reduced average API-equivalent cost from $0.38 to $0.15. Both settings found the complete answer key on these questions.
reports.limitation: One code-search dataset and software version; not evidence for delegating complex implementation to cheaper models.
reports.costContext: Opus lead with Haiku Explore workers; API-equivalent mean/run.

reports.title: Parallel research improved results with higher token usage
reports.summary: Anthropic reported a 90.2% improvement over single-agent Opus 4 on its internal research evaluation. It recommends independent research branches and notes substantial token overhead.
reports.limitation: Vendor internal evaluation on older models, not a general coding benchmark. The reported 15× token figure compares multi-agent work with chat, not single-agent research.

reports.title: Agent teams helped parallel tasks and hurt sequential tasks
reports.summary: Across 180 configurations, centralized teams improved a parallel financial-reasoning task by 80.9%; multi-agent variants reduced sequential planning performance by 39–70%.
reports.limitation: Architecture-level study across model families. It does not identify a universal best worker model or predict a particular project's savings.
